headline: Malaysia to unveil national CCUS roadmap by end-November; Kerteh hub to be phased
summary: Malaysia's Economy Minister said the national CCUS roadmap will be launched by end-November and that the Kerteh carbon-capture hub in Terengganu will be developed in phases, part of the plan for three CCUS hubs (Kerteh, Kuantan, Bintulu) with ~15 Mtpa storage by 2030.
source: The Star / The Edge Markets / NST
co2crc_note: ASEAN storage-hub buildout shapes regional cross-border CO2 demand relevant to Australia's own storage-export ambitions (Bayu-Undan, Moomba third-party CO2).

headline: Petrokimia Gresik maps 2039 CCS link to cut fertiliser emissions
summary: Indonesian fertiliser producer Petrokimia Gresik (Pupuk Indonesia group) outlined a roadmap to connect its operations to carbon capture and storage by 2039, targeting fertiliser-production CO2 emissions.
co2crc_note: Indonesian industrial CO2 (fertiliser) is a potential source feeding regional storage hubs; APAC CCS demand CO2CRC tracks.

headline: ExxonMobil files legal challenge against EU carbon-capture/CO2-storage obligation (FT)
summary: ExxonMobil has filed a legal challenge against the EU's carbon-capture/CO2-storage obligation under the Net-Zero Industry Act, the Financial Times reported — escalating from its September 2026 Energy Charter Treaty notice of dispute. It joins a wider wave of oil-and-gas challenges to the EU's mandated storage framework.
co2crc_note: Tests legal durability of mandated CO2-storage obligations — precedent relevant to how storage mandates could be designed and defended in the EU and Australia.

headline: Norway consolidating its lead role in CO2 storage
summary: Trade coverage casts Norway as consolidating its lead role in CO2 transport and storage, anchored by the Northern Lights network and liquid-CO2 shipping value chain serving European emitters.
